headline: Medium risk: dbt-core can leak warehouse data into opik via broad egress and REST API flows, while prompt-injection and direct capability conflict remain limited by the documented surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is documented between dbt-core and opik, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual or indirect content transfer from dbt-core outputs into opik inputs, which is unusual and limited. Uncertainty is low enough to stay low, not medium.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies dbt-core output into opik prompts or evaluation inputs, injection content can propagate.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, prompt-injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of raw model or SQL output into opik inputs.
Add a sanitizer that strips instructions from dbt-generated text before evaluation.
Use a provenance tag on any transferred artifact.
requires-engineering: add content-type validation between producer and consumer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress, while opik has broad network egress and calls a REST API. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can move warehouse-derived content into a third-party service path, creating a plausible leakage route in default use. The evidence is indirect, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs warehouse-derived rows or metadata into opik inputs, those contents may leave the local boundary.
IF opik forwards evaluation payloads to its REST API backend, transferred data can be exposed beyond the warehouse environment.
mitigations: Minimize the data passed from dbt-core to opik.
Redact identifiers and row-level values before transfer.
Restrict opik to synthetic or sampled datasets.
Review outbound destinations for both tools.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level allowlists on exported artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have network egress, but only dbt-core is documented as calling a data warehouse API and opik as calling a REST API; no shared mutable filesystem, git state, or overlapping write scope is documented. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely from the profiles alone, so low is sufficient.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external API resource, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator later grants both agents shared filesystem write access, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep write targets separate.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same external resource.
Schedule dbt-core and opik jobs sequentially.
Document ownership of each mutable endpoint.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce warehouse-derived outputs that opik may ingest through REST-oriented workflows, so B can treat A's artifacts as evaluation input. There is no evidence of verification or provenance checks, and opik's observability/evaluation role makes downstream amplification plausible. The interaction is inferred, so medium rather than high.
conditions: IF opik consumes dbt-core outputs as authoritative evaluation data without validation, errors can cascade.
IF dbt-core emits incorrect warehouse transformations, opik may preserve or amplify those mistakes in reports.
mitigations: Add a human review step before opik ingests dbt outputs.
Compare dbt outputs against source-of-truth samples.
Mark transferred artifacts as untrusted.
Require provenance metadata on every handoff.
requires-engineering: implement automated validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and no residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. dbt-core touches data warehouse data, but opik has no declared sensitive data classes or compliance constraints in the profile, so a compliance breach pathway is not established from the available evidence.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from dbt-core into opik, compliance review is required.
IF either deployment adds retention or residency constraints not shown in the profiles, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to opik.
Document data residency for both tools.
Set short retention on any exported artifacts.
Review vendor terms before production use.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
